# open-koumuten

*日本語*: [README.md](README.md)

AI-driven construction firm (working name). A Rust MVP that performs
**AI floor plan proposal generation and legal-violation checking**. It
receives site data from the sister repository
[open-fudousan](https://github.com/aon-co-jp/open-fudousan) (land/property
search) and integrates with
[open-cg-cad](https://github.com/aon-co-jp/open-cg-cad) (structural
analysis / seismic simulation) and
[aruaru-llm](https://github.com/aon-co-jp/aruaru-llm) (LLM inference
server).

## ⚠️ Important disclaimer (read first)

**Floor plan proposals generated by this system are drafts that stop one
step short of final review by a licensed professional (e.g. a licensed
architect). They are absolutely NOT a legally finalized design, nor
documents usable for an actual building permit application — review by a
licensed professional is always required.** This disclaimer text is
always included as `koumuten_core::DISCLAIMER_JA` in the `disclaimer`
field of every API response.

## Scope of this session (phase 1 of a staged rollout)

Per the user's explicit instruction, this phase is scoped strictly to
"AI floor plan proposal + legal-violation checking simulation".
**Electronic contracts, payments, and bookkeeping are a future phase and
are not implemented anywhere in this repository** (see "Deferred" below).

## Architecture

```
open-koumuten/
├── Cargo.toml (workspace)
├── crates/
│   ├── koumuten-core/   # floor plan generation, legal check, structural bridge, LLM comment core logic
│   └── koumuten-api/    # HTTP API (tokio/hyper directly, no web framework)
```

- Follows the ecosystem-wide convention: DB-independent, single-binary,
  no template engine (see `open-raid-z/CLAUDE.md`).
- `koumuten-core` calls `cg-cad-core` (`open-cg-cad`) as a **direct crate
  path dependency** (in-process, not inter-process HTTP — see
  "Integration with open-cg-cad" below for why).
- `koumuten-core::llm_comment` calls `aruaru-llm`'s `POST /v1/generate`
  over **real inter-process HTTP** (blocking `reqwest`). On connection
  failure it falls back to a fixed-text comment, so this repository can
  be exercised end-to-end even without `aruaru-llm` running.

## Build & run

```sh
cargo build --workspace --release
cargo test --workspace --release
./target/release/koumuten-api   # listens on http://127.0.0.1:8090 by default
                                 # (override with KOUMUTEN_PORT)
```

`aruaru-llm`'s URL defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:4600`
(override with `KOUMUTEN_ARUARU_LLM_URL`). `koumuten-api` works correctly
even if `aruaru-llm` is not running — the `llm_comment` field will contain
a fixed-text fallback that explicitly states the connection failed.

## API

- `POST /v1/proposals` — accepts site data (see "Input shape" below),
  generates multiple floor plan proposals, runs legal checks, runs a
  structural check on compliant proposals only, and generates an LLM
  comment, all in one call.
- `GET /healthz` — health check.

### Input shape (compatible with open-fudousan's `export-for-cad`)

Designed to be field-compatible with the JSON returned by
`open-fudousan`'s `GET /v1/properties/:id/export-for-cad`
(`open-fudousan` itself was not modified for this). In addition, this
repository proposes a new field not present in `open-fudousan`:
**`road_frontage_m`** (length of the site edge touching a public road, in
meters), needed for the road-frontage legal check. If omitted, that check
is skipped rather than assumed compliant (see `koumuten-core::site_input`
docs).

```json
{
  "property_id": "dummy-001",
  "site": { "vertices": [[0.0,0.0], [10.0,0.0], [10.0,10.0], [0.0,10.0]] },
  "zoning": { "building_coverage_ratio": 0.6, "floor_area_ratio": 2.0 },
  "site_area_m2": 100.0,
  "is_dummy_data": true,
  "road_frontage_m": 4.0
}
```

## What is implemented (scope disclosed honestly)

1. **Floor plan generation** (`koumuten-core::floor_plan`): generates
   several candidate plans from the site's bounding box, coverage ratio,
   floor-area ratio, and floor count. Room placement is a simple grid
   subdivision of the footprint rectangle — not a real design (no
   circulation planning, no orientation-aware daylight design).
2. **Legal check** (`koumuten-core::legal_check`): only these 3 checks are
   implemented (does **not** cover the full Building Standards Act,
   disclosed honestly):
   - Building coverage / floor-area ratio overrun (reuses `cg-cad-core::zoning`)
   - Simplified road-frontage check (`road_frontage_m >= 2.0m` only;
     road width/classification is not verified)
   - Simplified daylight-regulation check (flags a habitable room only
     when it touches none of the footprint's outer walls; does not
     compute effective daylight area ratios)
3. **Structural check** (`koumuten-core::structural_check`): calls
   `cg-cad-core`'s `generate_building` + `analyze_structure` as a direct
   crate dependency. **Honest disclosure**: `cg-cad-core` recomputes its
   own footprint from the site/zoning/floor count, so it is an
   approximation rather than an exact structural check of the proposal's
   own footprint. Inter-process HTTP was not used because `open-cg-cad`
   does not yet expose an HTTP API.
4. **LLM comment** (`koumuten-core::llm_comment`): calls `aruaru-llm`'s
   `POST /v1/generate` (GPT-2 124M) to produce a friendly user-facing
   comment. Falls back to fixed text on failure (verified working with
   `aruaru-llm` not running).
5. **Disclaimer**: always present in the `disclaimer` field of every API
   response.

## Verification results

- `cargo build --workspace --release` — succeeds, no warnings.
- `cargo test --workspace --release` — 16 tests in `koumuten-core` + 7 in
  `koumuten-api`, **23 total, all passing**.
- Real HTTP verification via a running server + PowerShell
  `Invoke-WebRequest` — `/healthz` and `/v1/proposals` (including the
  fallback path with `aruaru-llm` not running, and confirming an
  over-coverage proposal is correctly excluded and skips the structural
  check).
- **Also verified with a real running `aruaru-llm` (actual GPT-2 124M
  weights)** — `/v1/proposals` returned a genuine LLM-generated comment
  (not the fallback text).

## Deferred (next phase, not implemented at all here)

- **Electronic contracts**: not implemented, explicitly out of scope.
- **Payments**: not implemented, same reason.
- **Bookkeeping**: not implemented, same reason.
- **Comprehensive Building Standards Act coverage**: height limits,
  shadow regulations, setback-line (sky-exposure) regulations, fire
  zoning, and evacuation regulations are all unimplemented (also
  disclosed in the API's `not_checked_items` field).
- **Real architectural design**: circulation planning, window placement,
  and fire-resistance details are not modeled.
- **Changes to open-fudousan**: none were made, per instructions.
- **Inter-process HTTP for open-cg-cad**: deferred until `open-cg-cad`
  exposes an HTTP API of its own.

## Update 2026-08-23 — CPU SIMD applicability review (conclusion: not applicable, no code changes)

Alongside extending the shared
[`open-cpu`](https://github.com/aon-co-jp/open-cpu) crate, this repository
was reviewed for anything worth accelerating.
**Conclusion: nothing in this repository itself qualifies.**

Reasons, based on reading the actual code:

- About 1,150 lines of Rust across two crates: `koumuten-core` (floor-plan
  proposals, legality checks, structural checks, LLM commentary) and
  `koumuten-api` (HTTP directly on hyper, port 8090).
- The search in `floor_plan.rs` is a nested loop over floor-count and
  coverage-fraction candidates — on the order of a dozen combinations.
  `layout_rooms` splits a footprint into roughly six rooms per floor, and
  the loops in `legal_check.rs` run over well under a hundred elements.
- The only genuinely numeric work, structural analysis, is delegated from
  `structural_check.rs` to `cg-cad-core::analyze_structure` — it **is not
  computed in this repository**. Optimizing it therefore belongs in
  `open-cg-cad`, and indeed that is where this session's optimization was
  made (tunnel micro-pressure-wave index, O(n^2) → O(n)).

No `open-cpu` dependency was added. Revisit this section if floor-plan
search is ever extended from exhaustive enumeration to a real optimizer
(e.g. genetic algorithms) with candidate counts in the tens of thousands.
